newsitem.title: PANAMA: Two more firms eye Panama's state phone sale.
newsitem.headline: Two more firms eye Panama's state phone sale.

text.p: European international firms Cable and Wireless Plc and Telefonica de Espana SA presented pre-qualification documents Tuesday to take part in the sale of Panama's state telephone utility.
In a public act, they submitted documents for the sale of the National Telecommunications Institute (INTEL), INTEL director general Juan Porras told reporters.
Panama extended the pre-qualification process until Tuesday and will qualify the eligible firms in about 15 days. A public bid is scheduled for early 1997.
GTE Corp of the United States is so far the only company qualified to participate.
Telefonica was allowed to participate in the second round because the Spanish government's remaining 21 percent stake in the telecom company will be put on sale next year, Porras said.
Telefonica had originally withdrawn its interest in entering the privatization process earlier this year after the Panamanian government decided to ban state-owned foreign corporations.

"Now it's up to the board of directors (of INTEL) to decide whether they qualify. They are allowed to participate in the pre-qualification based on the pre-condition that they will be privatized," Porras said.

The INTEL privatization went to a second round after the process was derailed when key bidder SBC Communications Inc pulled out, opting to participate in Brazil's more lucrative market, where at least 15 telecom sales are planned. INTEL's value is estimated at $2 billion with assets of $450 million.
